q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
We are currently on 2026-08-24. NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings release has already occurred (the forward guidance was issued on May 20, 2026 at $91.0B ±2%). The question asks what the forward guidance *will be* in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release, which suggests this is asking about guidance that was already provided. Based on the research, the forward guidance has already been issued and is known: **$91.0 billion ±2%** (range: $89.2B to $92.8B).

However, the question phrasing "What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance" in future tense is ambiguous—it could be asking:
1. What was the actual forward guidance released? (Already known: $91.0B ±2%)
2. What will be the actual reported revenue for Q2 FY2027? (Different question)

Given the phrasing "forward guidance...in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release," I interpret this as asking: **What revenue figure was/will be provided as forward guidance when Q2 FY2027 results are announced.**

The research explicitly states this guidance was issued on May 20, 2026: **$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%**.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why
The most likely outcome is that the forward guidance will be **$91.0 billion** (the midpoint of the ±2% range). This is the explicit guidance NVIDIA provided on May 20, 2026, according to the research. The ±2% represents uncertainty, with the range being $89.2B to $92.8B.

The research indicates:
- NVIDIA's official guidance is $91.0B ±2%
- Wall Street's average estimate is ~$91.9B (slightly above guidance, within the range)
- Q1 FY2027 exceeded guidance by ~$2B, so Q2 could outperform similarly
- The company explicitly noted this assumes zero Data Center compute revenue from China

## (c) What would push the value lower?
- Weaker-than-expected demand for AI accelerators
- China export restrictions tightening further (already factored in at $0)
- Macro slowdown reducing customer capex
- Inventory corrections among customers
- Competitive pressure from AMD or other providers

## (d) What would push the value higher?
- Stronger-than-expected AI demand (as seen in Q1 with ~$2B outperformance)
- Better-than-expected customer demand despite China restrictions
- Pricing power maintenance in a competitive environment
- Unexpected revenue from other segments (professional visualization, automotive, etc.)

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values
The research directly provides NVIDIA's forward guidance issued on May 20, 2026:
- **Official guidance: $91.0 billion ±2% (range: $89.2B to $92.8B)**
- Q1 FY2027 actual: $81.6B (outperformed guidance by ~$2B)
- Wall Street consensus: ~$91.9B

This is not a prediction question—the forward guidance has already been issued and is documented in the research.

---

**Reasoning for distribution:**

Since the forward guidance was officially stated as $91.0B ±2%, the most likely point estimate is $91.0B. The range of $89.2B to $92.8B represents NVIDIA's official uncertainty band. There's a small tail risk that reported guidance could be slightly different from what the research states, but the research is explicit and sourced to SEC filings.

I'll center my distribution on $91.0B with tails extending toward the ±2% bounds, acknowledging that the actual guidance figure is already known but the question's future tense creates slight ambiguity.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, predicts $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027). This implies a range between $89.2 billion and $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). The company explicitly stated that this outlook assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm).

Wall Street analysts' average estimate is approximately $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), which falls within NVIDIA's guided range. For Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported $81.6 billion in revenue, exceeding its own guidance by about $2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). A similar outperformance in Q2 could push revenue near $95 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). The company also expects GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins to be around 74.9% and 75.0%, respectively [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027).
